reasons.B: Long, semicolon-jointed paragraphs and blunt, unhedged verdicts ('snobbery turned inside out, and quite as tiresome') match the passage's asserting, faintly contemptuous period voice without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Good period diction and semicolon series ('so has philosophy; so, most of all, has fiction') close to the passage, but the stacked exclamations and parenthetical aside push towards caricature.
reasons.D: Right era and dashes, but the wry, gentle turns ('and then one sits down', repeated rhetorical questions) are more genial and whimsical than the passage's flat, sharp assertion.
reasons.A: Plain modern register, short even sentences, no semicolons or dashes and a measured, hedged tone; reads as a present-day summary, not the author.
